title: Factorial Sandwich
statement: Notice that $6! = 8\cdot 9\cdot 10$. Find the largest positive integer $n$ for which $n!$ can be written as the product of $n - 3$ consecutive positive integers.
hints: Write the product of $n-3$ consecutive integers as $\dfrac{(n-3+k)!}{k!}$.
Then $\dfrac{(n-3+k)!}{n!} = k!$. Which $k$ allows $n$ to be large?
solution: We need $(n+1)(n+2)\cdots(n+k-3) = k!$ for some $k \ge 4$. The left side is a product of $k-3$ factors each larger than $n$. With $k=4$ it reads $n+1 = 24$, so $n = 23$, and indeed $23! = \frac{24!}{4!} = 5\cdot 6\cdots 24$. For $k \ge 5$, the left side grows with $n$, and at $n = 23$ it equals $\frac{(k+20)!}{23!} = k!\cdot\binom{k+20}{20}\big/(21\cdot 22\cdot 23)$. At $k = 5$ that ratio is $53130/10626 = 5$, and it only increases with $k$, so the left side already exceeds $k!$ at $n = 23$. Every solution with $k \ge 5$ therefore has $n < 23$.
